title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00480
what_is_it: FAA Washington Operations Center preliminary incident report documenting a UAP sighting by a commercial aircraft crew.
core_summary: On February 20, 2023, Ravn Alaska Flight 140, a De Havilland DH8A flying from Anchorage to Kenai, Alaska, reported a UAP while southwestbound at 6,000 feet, approximately 52 nautical miles northwest of Kenai. The crew described the UAP as a round black object that was stationary at approximately 16,000 feet. No evasive action was taken and Alaska NORAD Region was notified.

public_headline: Alaska Airline Crew Reported Stationary Black Object at 16,000 Feet
public_tldr: This FAA preliminary incident report documents a UAP sighting by the crew of Ravn Alaska Flight 140 on 20 February 2023. While flying at 6,000 feet near Kenai, Alaska, the crew observed a round black object hovering at approximately 16,000 feet; no evasive action was taken and Alaska NORAD Region was notified.
public_narrative:
This document is a preliminary incident report from the FAA Washington Operations Center, filed on 20 February 2023 at 6:59 PM Alaska Standard Time. It records a UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena) sighting reported by a commercial flight crew in Alaskan airspace.

Ravn Alaska Flight 140, a De Havilland DH8A turboprop flying from Anchorage to Kenai, was heading southwest at 6,000 feet, approximately 52 nautical miles northwest of Kenai. The crew reported observing a round black object that appeared stationary at roughly 16,000 feet — about 10,000 feet above their own altitude. No evasive action was taken.

Anchorage ARTCC (Air Route Traffic Control Center) was advised, and the Alaska NORAD Region — the military command responsible for North American aerospace defence in that area — was notified. The report does not mention any radar contact or sensor data corroborating the visual sighting.

This is a preliminary report only. No follow-up investigation, identification, or resolution is documented in this record. The object remains unidentified based on the information available here.
public_caveats: This is a single-source report based entirely on the flight crew's visual observation — no radar or sensor corroboration is mentioned.
It is a preliminary report only; no follow-up investigation or final determination is documented.
The altitude of the object (approximately 16,000 feet) is the crew's estimate, not an instrument-verified measurement.
The document shows low evidence of redaction, but the absence of further detail may simply reflect the preliminary nature of the report.
The report documents what was observed and reported — it does not identify the object or draw any conclusions about what it was.
